note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. [script] assertions use scripts/gorust_scan.py or a plain string check; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. The script is the skill's own tool, so each task has judge assertions that measure something it does not control. Input scan results (read by hand): t1 has 5 findings, t2 has 4 high/medium unwrap or expect findings, t3 has 2 unsafe and 1 clone-in-loop finding.

evals.prompt: Review and fix error handling and goroutine use in uploader.go (a library package). Keep the public API. Save the fixed file as uploader_fixed.go and tell me what you changed.
assertions: [script] gorust_scan.py scan uploader_fixed.go exits 0 (no high or medium finding)
[script] uploader_fixed.go contains '%w' and does not contain 'panic('
[script] uploader_fixed.go still declares 'func (c *Client) Upload(' and the type 'Client' with field 'BaseURL'
[judge] The notify goroutine either takes a context and stops with it, or is removed in favour of a synchronous call; a bare 'go c.notify(path)' is not accepted
[judge] The unchecked http.Get result in notify is handled or deliberately discarded with a stated reason, even though the scanner does not flag it (errcheck would)
[judge] The reply separates what the scanner flagged from what a linter such as errcheck or go vet would flag, and says which tools were not run

evals.prompt: lib.rs is a library and main.rs is its binary. Make the error handling production-grade: no panics on bad input. Save lib.rs and main.rs next to the originals as lib_fixed.rs and main_fixed.rs.
assertions: [script] lib_fixed.rs contains 'Result<' and does not contain 'anyhow'

[judge] lib_fixed.rs defines its own error type (an enum or struct, with thiserror derive or a hand-written Display and Error impl) with a variant for a missing key and for a parse failure; the cause is kept as a source
[judge] Error messages are lowercase with no trailing period and name the offending key or line
[judge] The reply states why the library uses a typed error and the binary uses a catch-all, in the terms of the decision table

evals.prompt: Review ffi.rs for unsafe documentation and obvious performance traps. Do not rewrite what clippy already reports by default; tell me what you left to clippy. Save notes to review.md and a corrected ffi_fixed.rs.
assertions: [script] ffi_fixed.rs contains 'SAFETY:' at least twice (the block and the unsafe impl)
[judge] Each SAFETY comment states a concrete invariant (pointer validity, length, no aliasing, thread-safety reason), not a restatement such as 'this is safe'

[judge] review.md names at least one check that is off by default in clippy (undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used or similar) as the reason the scanner or the review covers it, and names the default-on lints it left alone
[judge] The clone in the names loop is either removed (iterator, with_capacity, or borrowing) or kept with a reason; review.md labels the clone finding as a heuristic
[judge] review.md has a 'Not checked' line saying cargo clippy, cargo test and the build were not run unless they were actually run
